description: A tester for the SIMM, SIPP, DIP and ZIP memory of machines from the 1970s to the 1990s.
author: belikh

glossary.Base unit: The main board in its tray and console: processor, FPGA, power supplies, display, keys and the cartridge slot.
glossary.Cartridge: An adapter board in a printed shell that carries the sockets and buffers for one memory family. It slides into the base unit from the rear.
glossary.DUT: Device under test: the memory module or chip in a cartridge socket.
glossary.VDUT: The supply rail of the device under test. The base unit sets it between 2.3 V and 5.6 V and measures its current.
glossary.Tick: Half a clock period of the timing engine: 3.077 ns at 162.5 MHz. Every bus edge is placed to one tick.
glossary.March element: One pass over an address range that does up to six read or write operations at each address.
glossary.Timing engine: The FPGA logic that drives the memory bus, places every edge and compares what it reads.
